skill.name: emil-design-eng
skill.description: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
skill.summary: Guides polished, accessible, and performant interface motion through practical UI review principles.
skill.author: emilkowalski

content.value_statement: Interfaces often work correctly but still feel slow, inconsistent, or unclear. This skill reviews interaction details and recommends purposeful, accessible, performant motion.
actual_capabilities: Reviews UI code using a Before, After, and Why comparison table.
Selects animation purpose, easing, and duration according to interaction frequency.
Suggests CSS, React, Motion, and Web Animations API patterns for common interactions.
Evaluates transform, opacity, layout, and main-thread animation performance.
Checks reduced-motion behavior, touch hover handling, gesture damping, and pointer capture.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not render or test the interface.
Uses a specific design philosophy that may conflict with existing product conventions.
Browser and animation-library behavior can change, so technical claims require current verification.
Does not replace accessibility testing, performance profiling, or user research.

use_cases.title: Refine a component
use_cases.description: Review an existing button, dropdown, modal, or tooltip and receive prioritized motion improvements.

use_cases.title: Shape product motion
use_cases.description: Choose animation purpose, duration, easing, and reduced-motion behavior before implementation.

use_cases.title: Standardize interactions
use_cases.description: Create consistent animation rules and review criteria across reusable components.

prompt_templates.title: Review a button
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this button interaction for press feedback, duration, easing, and reduced motion: [describe behavior or paste relevant code].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one interactive element.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this dropdown animation with these design principles and return the required Before, After, and Why table: [details].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a component animation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a gesture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a swipe-to-dismiss interaction for [component], covering velocity, damping, pointer capture, touch handling, and interruption.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a gesture-driven component.

prompt_templates.title: Audit product motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [interface or code] for purpose, frequency, cohesion, accessibility, performance, and implementation tradeoffs. Prioritize the highest-impact changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a broader product experience.

output_examples.input: A dropdown uses a 400ms ease-in transition and scales from zero.
output_examples.output: The review recommends a shorter ease-out transition, a near-full starting scale, opacity support, and an origin tied to the trigger.

output_examples.input: A drawer updates an inherited CSS variable on every pointer movement.
output_examples.output: The audit identifies broad style recalculation and recommends updating the drawer transform directly while preserving damping and reduced-motion behavior.

output_examples.input: A toolbar animates every keyboard command and tooltip.
output_examples.output: The response removes keyboard-triggered motion, keeps the first tooltip delay, and makes later tooltips immediate while the group remains active.

best_practices: Provide the component code, interaction frequency, and user goal.
State browser support, framework constraints, and existing design-system rules.
Test recommendations with reduced motion, touch input, slow motion, and performance tools.
anti_patterns: Do not add animation when frequent actions already feel immediate.
Do not apply example timings without checking product context and interaction frequency.
Do not treat visual polish as a substitute for accessibility or usability testing.

faq.question: Does this skill write implementation code?
faq.answer: It can propose CSS, React, Motion, and Web Animations API patterns when you provide context.

faq.question: What review format does it use?
faq.answer: UI reviews use a Before, After, and Why markdown table.

faq.question: Can it review existing components?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide relevant code, current behavior, usage frequency, and product constraints.

faq.question: Does it address reduced motion?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends removing movement while retaining useful opacity and color feedback.

faq.question: Can it replace browser testing?
faq.answer: No. Validate motion on target browsers, physical touch devices, and constrained hardware.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
